scope: Diff-anchored profile of the reward-claim / banking machinery (story-031).

commitsInRange.sourceImpact: All 57 added lines in src/PhlimboV3.sol come from this commit.

newStateVariables.name: unclaimablePhUSDOf
newStateVariables.purpose: Per-beneficiary bank of phUSD reward whose mint reverted inside _claimRewards.
newStateVariables.keying: NOT token-keyed. Justified: phUSD is constructor-assigned and has no setter (verified).

newStateVariables.name: totalUnclaimablePhUSD
newStateVariables.purpose: Aggregate of the phUSD bank across all users. Purely informational: nothing is custodied against it because the tokens were never minted.
newStateVariables.capInteraction: None. phUSD emission is uncapped minting, not drawn from a distributable pool, so there is no ':789'-style cap adjustment as was required for the stable bank.

newFunctions.name: claimUnclaimablePhUSD()
newFunctions.note: Deliberately NOT whenNotPaused: beginFlush pauses the contract, so a gate would lock users out of self-rescue for the whole flush window. Mirrors claimUnclaimableStable / claimUnclaimablePromo.

changedControlFlow._claimRewards: phUSD mint leg (line 913) wrapped in try/catch. On catch: credit unclaimablePhUSDOf[beneficiary], increment totalUnclaimablePhUSD, emit PhUSDMintFailed. Previously a bare phUSD.mint() that propagated the revert and bricked the whole principal path.
changedControlFlow.batchClaim: UNCHANGED in this range. Still banks promo via _tryTransfer at :506 into unclaimablePromoOf/totalUnclaimableOf (story-027, audit-08 M-01). batchClaim never touches the phUSD or stable legs.
changedControlFlow.bankingHelpers: No new shared helper. The phUSD leg uses try/catch rather than the existing _tryTransfer (:971) because IFlax.mint returns void and _tryTransfer is a bool-decoding ERC20.transfer wrapper.

diffCharacterization.interfaceDelta: IPhlimboV3.sol adds the two events, the claimUnclaimablePhUSD() declaration, and the unclaimablePhUSDOf/totalUnclaimablePhUSD view getters. Additive only — no signature changed or removed, so no ABI break for existing integrators.

threeValueOutLegs.note: Line numbers are ACTUAL at HEAD f279c62 and have shifted from the historical values in the task prompt. Actual leg ORDER in _claimRewards is phUSD -> stable -> promo.

legs.failureBehavior: CAUGHT and BANKED. Does not propagate.
legs.stateWrittenBefore: None inside _claimRewards. pendingPhUSDAmount is read-only-derived from userDetails.amount, accPhUSDPerShare, userDetails.phUSDDebt.
legs.stateWrittenAfter: None inside _claimRewards on the success path. On the catch path: unclaimablePhUSDOf[beneficiary], totalUnclaimablePhUSD. Debt realignment is done by the CALLER after _claimRewards returns.
legs.trigger: PhlimboV3 losing mint authority on phUSD (owner-privileged, fully recoverable).

legs.failureBehavior: CAUGHT and BANKED. Does not propagate.
legs.trigger: Recipient-blocklisting rewardToken (USDC-class). Note: USDC blocklists recipients; USDT does not (see audit-09 Q-03 mock mislabel).
legs.capNote: No ':789' cap change needed — banked stable was already accrued out of rewardBalance in _updatePool, so it is not part of the distributable balance and is never redistributed (audit-09 M-01).

legs.failureBehavior: CAUGHT and BANKED. Does not propagate.
legs.guardedBy: Whole block gated on address(promoToken) != address(0) at line 946.
legs.reservation: Banked promo lands in totalUnclaimableOf and is RESERVED from finalizePromotion's leftover sweep (:552-556).

threeValueOutLegs.conclusion: All three value-out legs in _claimRewards are now non-reverting and banked. story-031 closes the last propagating leg. No leg in the claim path can brick a user's principal path as of f279c62.

bankingMechanism.summary: Three parallel, independent per-beneficiary banks — one per asset class. Each records a failed payout and exposes a permissionless, un-pause-gated self-service pull.

banks.keyingJustification: VERIFIED: phUSD assigned only at constructor :243, no setter exists. Cannot rotate.
banks.retrievalAuth: msg.sender only — permissionless but strictly self-service. No pull-on-behalf.
banks.settlement: RE-MINTS. phUSD.mint(msg.sender, amount) at :649. Unique among the three: the tokens were NEVER minted, so the contract custodies nothing against this balance.
banks.custodyBacking: NONE — this is the key asymmetry vs the stable/promo banks.
banks.failedPullSemantics: Reverts (mint still unauthorized), leaving the bank intact. Matches claimUnclaimableStable recoverability.

banks.keyingJustification: rewardToken assigned only at constructor :244, no setter.
banks.settlement: rewardToken.safeTransfer(msg.sender, amount) :624 — reverting transfer, contract holds the tokens.
banks.custodyBacking: Contract-held rewardToken balance, already accrued out of rewardBalance.

banks.keyingJustification: REQUIRED: promoToken DOES rotate — set at :403 (startPromotion), cleared at :559 (finalizePromotion). Design is internally consistent.
banks.custodyBacking: Contract-held promo balance, reserved from finalizePromotion's sweep.

debtAlignmentInteraction.criticalFinding: NO cross-leg debt interference. _claimRewards writes NO debt fields at all.
debtAlignmentInteraction.mechanism: Verified by inspection of lines 895-963: there is no assignment to userDetails.phUSDDebt / stableDebt / promoDebt anywhere inside _claimRewards. Every one of the three legs computes its pending amount from a debt value that the leg never mutates. Legs are therefore mutually independent — banking on the phUSD leg cannot corrupt the stable or promo leg's pending computation, and vice versa.
debtAlignmentInteraction.callerCompleteness: VERIFIED: _claimRewards has exactly three call sites (708, 749, 806) and all three realign all three debts to the full accumulator immediately after it returns.
debtAlignmentInteraction.consequence: Debt realigns to the full accumulator identically on the paid path and the banked path. Pending therefore settles to zero either way, and the banked amount can never be double-credited. This is what makes banking safe without any debt bookkeeping inside the legs.
debtAlignmentInteraction.testConfirmation: test_revertingMint_claim_succeeds_and_banks asserts pendingPhUSD(alice) == 0 after a banked claim; test_bankedPhUSD_notRedistributed_toCostaker asserts a co-staker's pending is unchanged.

noUnboundedLoops.detail: Single loop at :495 inside batchClaim, bounded by maxIterations via the cursor/end pattern. finalizePromotion requires flushCursor == _stakers.length() (:548) rather than looping. No loop in the claim path.

checkedArithmetic.detail: pragma ^0.8.19, no unchecked blocks, no assembly in the claim/banking path. totalUnclaimablePhUSD -= amount (:648) is underflow-protected.

reentrancyGuarded.detail: claimUnclaimablePhUSD is nonReentrant AND checks-effects-interactions correct: bank zeroed (:647) and aggregate decremented (:648) BEFORE the mint (:649).

delegated: claim — all require msg.sender == user || msg.sender == migrator

initializerProtected.detail: Not upgradeable. Constructor-based, with zero-address checks on _phUSD and _rewardToken (:240-241).

weakRandomness.detail: block.timestamp / block.number used only for reward accrual timing and the setDesiredAPY two-step commit window. No value-bearing entropy source.

inboundCallbackSurface.detail: No ERC721/1155/777 hooks. The only inbound-callback surface is the optional IPhlimboHook (onDeposit/onWithdraw/onClaim), invoked AFTER all state writes in stake/withdraw/claim, and the phUSD.mint / ERC20.transfer legs themselves.

claimPathInvariants.statement: A user's principal is never frozen by a failing reward payout.
claimPathInvariants.basis: All three value-out legs (913, 930, 954) are non-reverting and banked. story-031 closed the last propagating leg (phUSD mint). withdraw() reaches its principal safeTransfer at :774 regardless of any leg failing.
claimPathInvariants.testEvidence: test_revertingMint_withdraw_returns_principal_and_banks asserts phUSD.balanceOf(alice) == balBefore + STAKE_AMOUNT with the mint reverting.

claimPathInvariants.statement: banked + paid == earned, per user per asset.
claimPathInvariants.basis: Each leg either pays pendingX in full or banks pendingX in full — there is no partial path and no amount is dropped. The caller then realigns the debt to the full accumulator, so earned is accounted exactly once.

claimPathInvariants.statement: Debt alignment matches value actually delivered-or-banked.
claimPathInvariants.basis: Debt realignment is unconditional and caller-side, and is identical on the paid and banked paths. Because banking is in-full, 'delivered-or-banked' always equals the pending that the realignment discharges.
Incremented together (:915-916), decremented by exactly `amount` on pull (:647-648). The aggregate is never zeroed wholesale — it spans all users. Correct.

claimPathInvariants.statement: A banked phUSD amount is never redistributed to other stakers.
claimPathInvariants.basis: phUSD emission is uncapped minting driven by accPhUSDPerShare, not drawn from a finite distributable pool. Banking does not return value to any pool. Structurally distinct from the stable bank, which required the audit-09 M-01 no-redistribution reasoning.

claimPathInvariants.statement: A failed bank pull leaves the bank intact (recoverable).
claimPathInvariants.basis: claimUnclaimablePhUSD reverts atomically if the mint is still unauthorized, rolling back the :647-648 writes.
claimPathInvariants.testEvidence: test_claimUnclaimablePhUSD_roundTrip asserts bank intact after a failed pull, then full re-mint after authority restore.

claimPathInvariants.statement: The un-token-keyed banks are safe because their asset cannot rotate.
claimPathInvariants.basis: phUSD (:243) and rewardToken (:244) are constructor-only with no setter — verified by grep. promoToken DOES rotate (:403 / :559), which is exactly why unclaimablePromoOf is token-keyed. Design is internally consistent. See LOCAL-002: the invariant rests on absence-of-setter rather than the `immutable` keyword.

localFindings.description: The phUSD bank credits `beneficiary`, which under migrator delegation is the migrator (stake/withdraw/claim all pass msg.sender as beneficiary at 708/749/806). The only retrieval path, claimUnclaimablePhUSD() :644, is strictly msg.sender-keyed with no pull-on-behalf. A beneficiary that cannot itself originate a call to PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimablePhUSD() therefore has no retrieval path for its bank. Unlike the stable/promo banks, the phUSD bank is un-minted, so it is not reachable by a balance-sweeping escape hatch either.
localFindings.relationship: Extends the surface of the existing audit-10 finding V3-L-15 (migrator no-self-pull) to a THIRD asset. Do NOT treat as a fresh root cause — same class, new leg.
localFindings.boundaryNote: MigratorV2V3 exposes claimUnclaimable(address token) for its OWN internal forward-failure bank and an onlyOwner withdrawAll, but no call-through to PhlimboV3's claimUnclaimable* pulls. Confirming whether the migrator can reach this bank is an INTERACTION-level question — deliberately not adjudicated here.
localFindings.recommendation: Either add a pull-on-behalf variant, or confirm the migrator is never a live beneficiary of a failing mint. Route to interaction analysis together with V3-L-15.

localFindings.description: The NatSpec at :168-171 justifies the un-token-keyed phUSD bank with 'phUSD is fixed at construction and never rotates'. That is true today, but `IFlax public phUSD` (:51) and `IERC20 public rewardToken` (:55) are plain storage, not `immutable`. The safety of both un-keyed banks rests on the continued absence of a setter rather than on a compiler guarantee — a future setter would silently strand every banked balance under the old asset.
localFindings.recommendation: Declare phUSD and rewardToken `immutable` so the banks' keying invariant is enforced by the compiler. Zero runtime cost; also saves an SLOAD per claim.

localFindings.description: foundry.toml now sets optimizer=true, optimizer_runs=10000, via_ir=false, with an inline comment stating via_ir is disabled because it collapses repeated vm.warp calls in tests, and that 'Deploying with via_ir is safe'. If deployment ever uses via_ir=true, the deployed bytecode is produced by a different codegen pipeline than the bytecode the entire test suite exercises. The tests would not have validated the deployed artifact.
localFindings.unverifiedClaim: The comment's EIP-170 claim (~16 KB, +8.6 KB margin under legacy+optimizer) was NOT independently verified here — building would write to the read-only submodule's out/. Downstream should confirm from workspace/.
localFindings.recommendation: Pin the deployment profile to the same codegen as the tested profile, or add a [profile.deploy] and a size check in CI. Fix the test-side vm.warp interaction rather than diverging the pipelines.

localFindings.description: RewardsClaimed(user, pendingPhUSDAmount, pendingRewardAmount) is emitted at :939 whenever either amount is non-zero, including when that value was BANKED rather than paid. An indexer sees both RewardsClaimed and PhUSDMintFailed/StableClaimFailed for the same value and may double-count distributed rewards. Pre-existing for the stable leg; story-031 extends the ambiguity to phUSD.
localFindings.note: Accounting is correct on-chain — this is an off-chain observability issue only.
localFindings.recommendation: Emit RewardsClaimed with the amounts actually delivered, or document that RewardsClaimed means 'settled (paid or banked)'.

externalEntryPoints.notes: Rewards route to msg.sender, NOT user — migrator delegation lands rewards (and banks) in the migrator.
Principal transfer at :774 is UNCONDITIONALLY reached — no reward leg can block it. Dust rule forces full exit below MINIMUM_STAKE.
Snapshots pending BEFORE _claimRewards to feed the hook exact amounts. Hook receives the amounts EARNED, which may have been banked rather than paid.
NEW in story-031. RE-MINTS. CEI-correct. Reverts 'Nothing to claim' on empty bank; reverts on still-missing authority leaving bank intact.
UNCHANGED this range. Forces payout to the STAKER (not the caller), unlike _claimRewards which routes to beneficiary. Permissionless — see audit-09 V3-H-01 history re: accrual during Flushing.
beginFlush pauses the contract — the rationale for all three bank pulls being un-pause-gated.

Ejector seat BY DESIGN (story-022, terminal, recovery out-of-band). Sweeps the ENTIRE phUSD/rewardToken/promo balances including principal and live banks. Per project precedent, do NOT propose accounting inside it.

externalEntryPoints.function: setMigrator / setHook / setPauser / setDesiredAPY / setDepletionDuration / setPromoDepletionDuration / startPromotion / topUpPromotion

externalCalls.notes: Constructor-fixed, no setter. Doubles as the STAKING token and a REWARD token. mint() returns void -> try/catch, not _tryTransfer. Mint authority is owner-managed and revocable — that revocation is precisely the banked path's trigger.
Constructor-fixed. Assumed USDC-class; recipient blocklisting is the modelled failure. USDC blocklists recipients, USDT does not (audit-09 Q-03).
Optional, zero-address guarded, owner-set. Invoked AFTER all state writes. A reverting hook WOULD brick stake/withdraw/claim — the banking work does not cover the hook leg. Interaction-level concern.

methods: inbound only — calls stake/withdraw/claim on behalf of users
externalCalls.notes: Owner-set delegate. Becomes `beneficiary` for delegated claims and therefore the credited party for any bank. See LOCAL-001.
Arbitrary caller address on self-service paths. All three legs are non-reverting, so a hostile recipient cannot brick the path — it can only force its own value into the bank.

stateVariables.name: totalUnclaimablePhUSD
stateVariables.notes: Not read by any accounting logic — informational only. No cap interaction.

stateVariables.name: userInfo
stateVariables.notes: CRITICAL: debts are mutated ONLY by the three external callers, never inside _claimRewards.

trustAssumptions: phUSD (IFlax) is a trusted, non-rotating token whose mint authority is owner-managed. Losing that authority is the ONLY trigger for the phUSD bank, and it is fully recoverable by re-granting.
rewardToken is USDC-class: standard ERC20 semantics plus possible recipient blocklisting. Fee-on-transfer is out of scope (C4 known-invalid).
promoToken is owner-chosen per promotion and may blocklist recipients.
The optional IPhlimboHook is trusted not to revert — the banking work does NOT protect the hook leg, which is invoked after state writes in stake/withdraw/claim.
emergencyTransfer is a terminal ejector seat by design (story-022); it sweeps live banks along with principal and is out-of-band recovery, not an accounting path.
The migrator is a trusted owner-set delegate. Its ability to retrieve a bank credited to it is an INTERACTION-level question (LOCAL-001).
deferredToInteractionAnalysis: Whether MigratorV2V3 can retrieve a phUSD/stable bank credited to it as beneficiary (LOCAL-001 / V3-L-15 class).
Whether a reverting IPhlimboHook can brick stake/withdraw/claim despite all three reward legs now being banked.
Interaction of a live phUSD bank with emergencyTransfer's terminal sweep (bank re-mints fresh supply post-sweep).
Whether the permissionless batchClaim's promo accrual interacts with the new phUSD bank (audit-09 V3-H-01 lineage) — no coupling found locally.

coverageNotes.harnessQuality: NOT vacuous. MockRevertingMintFlax genuinely reverts on mint while leaving transfers intact, so the banked path is actually exercised rather than trivially passing. Assertions check both per-user and aggregate bank state plus debt realignment to zero.
gaps: No test covers a migrator-as-beneficiary banked mint (LOCAL-001).
No stateful fuzz/invariant test over the new bank — consistent with the project's known lack of stateful fuzzing.
